text:
Ava (eng-runtime): Heads-up — our OTEL spans are spiking in unique attribute cardinality since the prompt-tracing change. Top offenders: prompt_text, user_id, request_id. Seeing a 5x cardinality bump in traces index.

Leo (eng-platform): Oof. Are we shipping raw prompt_text in span attributes right now?

Ava (eng-runtime): Yes, root cause: quick debug add. We pushed raw prompt_text into span attributes for a couple services.

Sam (eng-security): Please stop. Raw prompts can contain PII. We need immediate scrubbing.

Maya (eng-ml): For ML evals we sometimes need the original prompt. Can we instead store prompt_hash in spans and keep full prompt in a gated blob store (TTL + ACL)? That keeps telemetry safe and debuggable.

Leo (eng-platform): I agree. Also request_id is unique per request so it explodes cardinality. Options: drop request_id, replace with bucketed value, or only keep full request_id on sampled traces (e.g., error=true).

Nina (eng-sre): +1 to sampling. We should prefer attribute-based sampling: keep full ids when span.status != OK or error tags present; otherwise store hashed/truncated ids.

Ava (eng-runtime): Proposed short-term pipeline changes (can we do this in collector quickly?):
- Replace prompt_text -> prompt_hash (sha256 hex)
- Replace user_id -> user_bucket (HMAC with per-org key, mod 1000)
- request_id -> 8-char prefix + minute-bucket suffix OR only export full request_id for 1% sample
- Add attributes processor to drop any attribute matching /password|ssn|card/
- Retain hashed attributes for 30d, full debug blobs in blob-store for 7d

Sam (eng-security): Per-org HMAC key is critical. Deterministic salt across tenants would allow cross-tenant linking which is bad. We should store per-org HMAC keys in KMS and rotate quarterly.

Leo (eng-platform): Implementation sketch for otel-collector processor (very rough):
```yaml
processors:
  scrub_attrs:
    actions:
      - key: prompt_text
        action: hash
        hash: sha256
      - key: user_id
        action: hash_hmac
        hmac_key_ref: k8s://secret/telemetry-user-hmac
      - key: request_id
        action: truncate
        truncate_length: 8
      - key: request_id
        action: insert
        value: ${timestamp_minute_bucket}
      - key: password
        action: delete
```
(we'll need to wire HMAC keys in via secret mount)

Maya (eng-ml): For evals: we can write a small service that accepts prompt_hash -> returns full prompt if request has valid audit token and within TTL. Store blob-store entries with visibility metadata. That keeps telemetry index lean.

Ava (eng-runtime): Sampling policy thoughts: tail-based sampler to keep error traces + a small uniform head-sample for analytics. Also offer attribute-based sampler: keep full attributes if span.attributes.debug=true.

Nina (eng-sre): Runtime concerns: adding HMAC in collector could add CPU cost. Maybe do HMAC in the app layer for high-throughput paths and let collector be lighter weight. But we need a plan that works for private deployments too.

Sam (eng-security): If apps do HMAC, enforce library usage so keys never leave KMS in plaintext. We can provide a small SDK util.

Leo (eng-platform): Action items: 
- Ava: open a collector config PR with scrub_attrs processor + basic sampling (ETA: EOD tomorrow)
- Sam: design KMS key rotation + per-org key proposal (ETA: 2d)
- Maya: prototype prompt_hash->blob-store rehydration service (ETA: 1w)
- Nina: run perf test for HMAC in collector vs app + report (ETA: 3d)

Ava (eng-runtime): I'll also add a quick alert to limit cardinality: if unique_attr_cardinality > 1M in 1h, auto-roll back prompt_text attribute.

InfraBot: Alert scheduled: trace-cardinality-check will run hourly.

Leo (eng-platform): Thanks everyone. Prioritize security-first scrub + minimal perf impact. Ping me once the collector PR is up so I can review the exporter changes. :thumbsup:
